source_event.summary: Independent audit found a canonical HTTP entrypoint omitted from public-boundary classification while attack matrix and saturation agreed on the omission.

generalized_learning.generalized_failure_pattern: A canonical specification can contain a material HTTP entrypoint while downstream attack and saturation artifacts both omit the corresponding public-boundary family, allowing mutually consistent artifacts to certify an incomplete risk model.
generalized_learning.plausible_wrong_implementation: Derive risk saturation only from the already-authored attack matrix, so the same missing risk family disappears from both artifacts without any gate disagreement.
generalized_learning.prevention_rule: Rederive canonical risk signals directly from required textual specification sources; an explicit HTTP method plus route activates public-boundary independently of the attack matrix.
generalized_learning.detection_rule: Block handoff when a canonical HTTP entrypoint signal is absent from attack-matrix risk families, even if risk saturation mirrors the same omission.

transfer_cases.scenario: A synthetic GET route in a required canonical specification must activate public-boundary.
A synthetic POST callback route in a required canonical specification must activate public-boundary.

skill_changes.evidence: Canonical-source risk derivation and previously promoted restrictive selected-scope extraction are present; genericity gate passes.
Seven focused generic tests pass, including two public-boundary transfer surfaces and canonical obligation-drift rejection.
